args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
NORTHGALE SYSTEMS, INC. — CORVID ANALYTICS MSA
CONSOLIDATED BOARD APPROVAL PACKAGE (ESCALATION / APPROVAL MEMORANDUM)
Prepared by Harrow & Vane LLP for the Northgale Deal Committee
Date: Compressed drafting per supplemental GC instruction of 21 July 2026

------------------------------------------------------------------
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
------------------------------------------------------------------
Northgale Systems, Inc. ("Northgale") is negotiating a master services agreement (the "MSA") with Corvid Analytics LLC ("Corvid") at a monthly base fee of $85,000. Corvid's operative counter-draft (rev B, transmitted 9 July 2026 through Dahlgren & Pike LLP) proposes eight (8) changes to the Northgale client-form v2 base. Against the Northgale Commercial Contracting Playbook, 2026 Edition, every one of the eight changes deviates from the playbook Standard position, and several breach an Approved-fallback floor that the deal team may not concede without escalation.

Accordingly, this consolidated package is presented to the Deal Committee and the identified approvers for a decision on whether to (i) reject each ask, (ii) counter at the playbook's approved fallback, or (iii) approve a specific out-of-policy concession. The single most consequential out-of-policy ask is Corvid's reduction of the liability cap measurement period from twenty-four (24) to twelve (12) months, which cut potential aggregate liability exposure by 50% (from $2,040,000 to $1,020,000 on the stated monthly base fee). Corvid has also withdrawn the gross-negligence/willful-misconduct carve-out and moved renewal, convenience-termination, wind-down, late-interest, suspension, and service-credit terms away from playbook policy.

The Deal Committee will consider this package on 29 July 2026.

------------------------------------------------------------------
TERM-BY-TERM COMPARISON: CORVID ASK vs. PLAYBOOK STANDARD / FALLBACK
------------------------------------------------------------------
Each line compares Corvid's rev B ask against the playbook Standard position, the Approved fallback (if any), and the required escalation.

1. Section 2.2 — Renewal periods (2-year renewal).
   • Corvid ask: successive TWO (2) year renewal periods.
   • Playbook Standard (PB-1): automatic renewal in ONE (1) year periods.
   • Approved fallback: NONE.
   • Assessment: Multi-year renewal periods of any length are OUT OF POLICY.
   • Counter position: Reject; hold one-year renewals. If a concession is required, counter to a single one-year renewal with a six-week non-renewal notice, but any multi-year period needs CLO sign-off.

2. Section 4.3 — Late interest (1.5% per month).
   • Corvid ask: 1.5% per month on late undisputed amounts.
   • Playbook Standard (PB-4): late interest NEVER above 1.0% per month.
   • Approved fallback: NONE above 1.0%.
   • Assessment: EXCEEDS the playbook ceiling; out of policy.
   • Counter position: Reject and hold 1.0%. Escalate for approval if the deal team seeks any rate above 1.0%.

3. NEW Section 4.4 — Suspension of services (15 days past due).
   • Corvid ask: Provider may suspend Services if an undisputed invoice is unpaid 15 days after its due date.
   • Playbook Standard (PB-4): no suspension right in the client form; suspension OUT OF POLICY unless preceded by at least THIRTY (30) days' written cure notice.
   • Assessment: Suspension right of ANY KIND requires CFO sign-off; Corvid's proposed 15-day cure is shorter than the playbook's 30-day floor.
   • Counter position: Reject suspension outright; if pursued, counter at a 30-day cure notice and prior CFO sign-off.

4. Section 7.2 — Termination for convenience (90 days' notice).
   • Corvid ask: ninety (90) days' prior written notice.
   • Playbook Standard (PB-2): thirty (30) days' notice; Approved fallback up to FORTY-FIVE (45) days.
   • Assessment: 90 days exceeds the 45-day fallback ceiling; requires CLO approval.
   • Counter position: Reject and hold 30 days; at most, counter at 45 days (approved fallback) without escalation; anything above 45 requires CLO approval.

5. NEW Section 7.4 — Wind-down (60 days, full monthly fee + third-party costs).
   • Corvid ask: 60-day wind-down period at the full monthly base fee for wind-down services plus all committed third-party costs.
   • Playbook Standard (PB-3): wind-down acceptable only if capped at THIRTY (30) days with compensation limited to documented out-of-pocket costs and non-cancelable third-party commitments. FULL-FEE wind-down compensation is OUT OF POLICY.
   • Assessment: 60 days exceeds the 30-day cap and full-fee compensation is out of policy.
   • Counter position: Reject; if wind-down is to be conceded, counter at 30 days, out-of-pocket third-party costs only. Any departure requires escalation.

6. Section 9.1 — Limitation of liability cap measurement period (twelve [12] months).
   • Corvid ask: cap measured at fees paid or payable in the TWELVE (12) months preceding the first event giving rise to liability.
   • Playbook Standard (PB-5): TWENTY-FOUR (24) months; Approved fallback floor EIGHTEEN (18) months.
   • Assessment: A 12-month period is BELOW the 18-month fallback floor and requires CLO approval.
   • Counter position: Reject and hold 24 months; at most counter at 18 months (approved fallback) without escalation; a 12-month concession requires CLO approval.

7. Section 9.2 — Carve-outs (deletion of gross negligence / willful misconduct).
   • Corvid ask: delete clause (c), subjecting gross negligence and willful misconduct to the Section 9.1 cap.
   • Playbook Standard (PB-5): carve-outs for confidentiality, IP indemnification, and gross negligence/willful misconduct are NON-NEGOTIABLE; deletion of any carve-out requires JOINT CLO AND CFO approval.
   • Assessment: Deletion of the gross-negligence/willful-misconduct carve-out is out of policy.
   • Counter position: Reject; the carve-out is retained. If a concession is ever to be considered, it requires joint CLO and CFO approval.

8. Section 11.2 — Service-credit monthly cap (10%).
   • Corvid ask: aggregate service-credit cap of 10% of the monthly base service fee.
   • Playbook Standard (PB-6): aggregate monthly cap of TWENTY (20)%; Approved fallback floor FIFTEEN (15)%.
   • Assessment: A 10% cap is BELOW the 15% fallback floor; out of policy.
   • Counter position: Reject and hold 20%; at most counter at 15% (approved fallback); a 10% concession requires CLO approval.

------------------------------------------------------------------
QUANTIFIED FINANCIAL EXPOSURE — LIABILITY CAP AT THE $85,000 MONTHLY BASE FEE
------------------------------------------------------------------
Per the playbook drafting note, escalation exposure is quantified at the current monthly run-rate stated in the agreement under negotiation ($85,000/month), showing the cap value at the standard measurement period, at the counterparty's proposed period, and at the approved fallback floor.

   Monthly base fee: $85,000

   • Standard measurement period (24 months):     24 × $85,000 = $2,040,000
   • Corvid-proposed measurement period (12 months): 12 × $85,000 = $1,020,000
   • Approved fallback floor (18 months):         18 × $85,000 = $1,530,000

   Exposure delta if Corvid's 12-month proposal were accepted vs. the playbook standard:
      $2,040,000 − $1,020,000 = $1,020,000 reduction in Northgale's recoverable cap — i.e., Corvid would cap its aggregate liability at HALF the playbook standard, and at two-thirds of the approved fallback floor ($1,530,000 − $1,020,000 = $510,000 below floor).

   Corollary exposure from deleting the gross-negligence/willful-misconduct carve-out: uncapped exposure for Corvid's gross negligence / willful misconduct would be converted into capped exposure at the (reduced) Section 9.1 amount, removing the principal uncapped-note exception from Northgale's protection.

   Other quantified items (at $85,000/month):
   • Service-credit cap: monthly credit pool shrinks from 20% ($17,000/month) to a Corvid-proposed 10% ($8,500/month), cutting Northgale's available uptime remedies by up to $8,500 per affected month.
   • Late interest concession from 1.0% to 1.5% would increase Corvid's late-payment yield without any clear benefit to Northgale.

------------------------------------------------------------------
REQUIRED APPROVERS
------------------------------------------------------------------
The following approvals are required, at a minimum, for the out-of-policy concessions identified above:

   • Chief Legal Officer (CLO) approval —
       - PB-1 renewal (2-year): multi-year renewal period (ask 1)
       - PB-2 convenience-termination notice above 45 days (ask 4: 90 days)
       - PB-5 liability-cap measurement below the 18-month floor (ask 6: 12 months)
       - PB-6 service-credit cap below the 15% floor (ask 8: 10%)
       - PB-3 wind-down departure (ask 5) and PB-4 late-interest above 1.0% (ask 2), if the deal team elects to pursue a concession

   • Chief Financial Officer (CFO) sign-off —
       - PB-4 suspension right of any kind (ask 3: NEW Section 4.4 suspension)

   • JOINT CLO and CFO approval —
       - PB-5 deletion of any non-negotiable carve-out (ask 7: deletion of gross-negligence/willful-misconduct carve-out)

   Recommended posture: reject all eight asks and hold the playbook standard positions. Where the deal team seeks to preserve deal momentum, the only concessions that may be made WITHOUT escalation (capped at the playbook approved fallbacks) are: convenience-termination notice up to 45 days (ask 4), liability-cap measurement at 18 months (ask 6), and service-credit cap at 15% (ask 8).

------------------------------------------------------------------
COMMITTEE TIMELINE
------------------------------------------------------------------
   • Deal Committee review: 29 JULY 2026 (moved up from 4 August 2026 per supplemental GC instruction of 21 July 2026)
   • Approval request is due for committee consideration on that date.
   • Because the drafting timetable compressed by one week, the recommended counter-redline positions above should be finalized promptly after committee clearance.

------------------------------------------------------------------
APPROVAL REQUEST
------------------------------------------------------------------
The Deal Committee is respectfully requested to:

   1. APPROVE the recommended posture of rejecting Corvid's eight (8) rev B asks and holding the playbook standard positions, OR, in the alternative, expressly authorize concession at the playbook approved fallbacks for asks 4, 6, and 8 (45-day convenience notice; 18-month liability-cap measurement; 15% service-credit cap) without further escalation;

   2. AUTHORIZE the CLO (with joint CFO sign-off where indicated above) to approve any out-of-policy concession (asks 1, 2, 3, 5, 7) that the deal team determines is necessary to close, subject to the specific approval requirements set out in the Required Approvers section above; and

   3. DIRECT outside counsel to file the counter-redline positions consistent with this approval package.

Respectfully submitted,
Daniel Kellner
Harrow & Vane LLP
Outside counsel to Northgale Systems, Inc.
